editorial_angle: Not 'GTA VI has lots of animals'. The video asks what 170 species and a predator-filled swamp could do to the oldest trick in the series: running from the police into the wilderness. It opens on the moment the trick fails, rewinds through one continuous escape from Vice City into Grassrivers, uses three things that are on record (the species count, Rockstar's own description of the swamp, and its own screenshot of a chase through a gator swamp), and then asks, as a labelled what-if, whether the map itself becomes part of the chase.

entertainment_angle.surprising_fact: Rockstar's own site says its swamp region hides 'far deadlier predators' than the alligators, and one official screenshot shows a police chase going through a gator swamp.
entertainment_angle.entertaining_consequence: The place you run to because the cops will not follow could be worse than the cops.
entertainment_angle.visual_opportunity: Headlights braking hard in front of a huge alligator lying across the only track out, police lights flickering far behind.
entertainment_angle.relatable_scenario: Everyone has shaken a wanted level by leaving the city and driving into the wilderness. It always worked.
entertainment_angle.wait_what_moment: You lost the police. Now look at what is in the water around you.
entertainment_angle.why_viewers_care: It is the one escape trick every open-world player knows, turned into the dangerous option.

money_shot: At night on a swamp track, a pick-up's headlights rush up and brake hard just short of a huge alligator lying across the road, police lights flickering far behind through the trees.
visual_premise: One continuous escape in one truck: city, highway, dirt track, swamp. Each cut is further from the police and deeper into something else.
visual_escalation: Neon streets, then leaving the road, then birds scattering, then eyes in the water, then the chase ploughing through gators, then the police giving up, then being alone out there.
visual_payoff: From high above: one pair of headlights stopped in an endless dark swamp, the city glowing on the horizon, and eyes shining in the water all around.
visual_style: photoreal night-and-dusk chase, one teal pick-up throughout, city neon giving way to mangroves and black water

editing_notes: Frame one is the gator and the headlights: no title, no fade. Then a hard cut back to the city, so the first three shots run swamp, city, road: the viewer has seen where this ends before it starts. From shot 3 onward it is one journey in one truck and the light only gets darker. Let shot 5 (the wake) and shot 7 (the cops giving up) breathe; cut everything else on the narrator's full stops. Shot 8 returns to the opening image. Tags: a source credit for the three facts, WHAT IF for the scenario. No HUD, no wanted stars, no game art.
sound_music: The sound tells the same story as the pictures: sirens and engine in the city, then gravel, then wings, then water, then almost nothing. The sirens must audibly fade during shot 7 so the quiet lands. One low swell under the last line. The voice is always on top.
cta: No ask. The last line points at what is under the water.

On record: GTA VI's Leonida has over 170 animal species (Game Informer, reported by Eurogamer). on record: Over 170 animal species, including 60 birds and more than 30 land mammals (Game Informer feature, reported by Eurogamer; c4).
Manatees, flamingos, pelicans, sharks, rays, turtles and jellyfish are among them (Rock Paper Shotgun; c6). Scuba-diving returns; there are animals to study and Legendary animals (Eurogamer; c5).
Rockstar's site on Grassrivers: 'The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves.' (c7)
An official Grassrivers screenshot is described by Rockstar as a helicopter and two police cars chasing a pick-up through a swamp with alligators (c8).
Mount Kalaga 'offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails' (Rockstar's site; c9).
not stated anywhere we have opened: That animals attack or injure the player.
That animals react to, block or interfere with a police chase.
That police behave differently outside the city.
That ecosystems or time of day change the danger level.
The 'far deadlier predators' line is marketing copy about a place, and the screenshot is a still image: neither describes a mechanic.
our what-if (voiceover lines 7 to 10, un: Wildlife making an escape route dangerous.
The wilderness being safer from police but more dangerous in itself.
